name: Erosion Portraits
description: A formally radical neural-feed anthology in which five directors — each from a different tier of M88 society — were given identical neural-feed templates and asked to depict the same event: the demolition of the old Milwaukee transit hub in 2218. The viewer experiences all five perspectives simultaneously, their consciousness fragmenting across class positions, sensory contexts, and emotional registers. The experience of genuine cognitive dissonance as the film's POVs conflict is not a bug — it is the entire point.
cultural_impact: Erosion Portraits established multi-perspective simultaneous neural-feed as a legitimate art form and is credited with beginning a serious conversation about whose sensory experience is considered default in BCI entertainment design.
story_hooks: The Tier 1 director has been approached by someone who wants to fund a second anthology — this time documenting an event that hasn't happened yet, suggesting foreknowledge of planned corporate action.

The HelixCorp classification of the Tier 1 segment as incitement was based on a specific 4-second sequence; someone in the party has seen that sequence and can't stop thinking about what it actually shows.
A bootleg version of Erosion Portraits has been circulating with a sixth perspective spliced in — one that no director claims to have made, depicting the demolition from inside the walls.
